messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Young Japanese women with high depression scores (alone or together with high unidentified-complaint scores) had lower vitamin D intake than those with low scores.
Sentence: "Our findings indicate that participants with high scores for unidentified complaints, depression, or both had lower intake levels of eicosapentaenoic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, vitamin D, and vitamin B12 than those with low scores, alongside reduced fish and shellfish consumption."
Measured as: depression score (questionnaire)
Population: Young Japanese women in a cross-sectional questionnaire survey
Intervention: Dietary vitamin D intake (assessed by questionnaire)
Comparator: Participants with low depression scores
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A is a single-arm case series of a combination supplement (vitamin D3 plus folic acid and B12) with no comparator, while Study B is a cross-sectional survey linking dietary vitamin D intake to depression scores; both bear on vitamin D and depression, and the designs differ most.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","comparator","outcome_measure"],"detail":"design: uncontrolled single-arm case series of a D3+folate+B12 supplement in elderly Parkinson's patients vs cross-sectional dietary intake survey in young Japanese women"}
